import type {
  RuleConditionEntity,
  SummaryContent,
  SummaryWidget,
  TimeFrame,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import {
  toComparableConditions,
  toComparableTimeFrame,
} from '#components/reports/widgetModified';

type SummaryMeta = NonNullable<SummaryWidget['meta']>;

export type SummaryWidgetSettings = Required<
  Pick<SummaryMeta, 'conditions' | 'conditionsOp' | 'timeFrame' | 'content'>
>;

const DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT: SummaryContent = {
  type: 'sum',
  divisorAllTimeDateRange: false,
  divisorConditions: [],
  divisorConditionsOp: 'and',
} as SummaryContent;

/** Reads the saved "Show as" settings, falling back to a plain sum. */
export function parseSummaryContent(content?: string): SummaryContent {
  if (!content) {
    return DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT;
  }
  try {
    return JSON.parse(content);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to parse widget meta content:', error);
    return DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT;
  }
}

/** The settings "Save widget" writes for a Summary widget. */
export function buildSummaryWidgetSettings({
  conditions,
  conditionsOp,
  start,
  end,
  mode,
  content,
}: {
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[];
  conditionsOp: 'and' | 'or';
  start: string;
  end: string;
  mode: TimeFrame['mode'];
  content: SummaryContent;
}): SummaryWidgetSettings {
  return {
    conditions,
    conditionsOp,
    timeFrame: { start, end, mode },
    content: JSON.stringify(content),
  };
}

function toComparableSummaryContent(content?: string) {
  const parsed = parseSummaryContent(content);
  const type = parsed.type ?? 'sum';
  if (type !== 'percentage' || parsed.type !== 'percentage') {
    // The divisor settings only apply to percentages, and the report resets
    // the divisor filters when it opens with any other type.
    return { type, fontSize: parsed.fontSize };
  }
  return {
    type,
    fontSize: parsed.fontSize,
    ...(({ conditions, conditionsOp }) => ({
      divisorConditions: conditions,
      divisorConditionsOp: conditionsOp,
    }))(
      toComparableConditions(
        parsed.divisorConditions,
        parsed.divisorConditionsOp,
      ),
    ),
    divisorAllTimeDateRange: parsed.divisorAllTimeDateRange ?? false,
  };
}

export function toComparableSummarySettings(
  meta: Partial<SummaryMeta> | null | undefined,
) {
  return {
    ...toComparableConditions(meta?.conditions, meta?.conditionsOp),
    // Without a saved time frame the report shows all time.
    timeFrame: toComparableTimeFrame(meta?.timeFrame, { mode: 'full' }),
    content: toComparableSummaryContent(meta?.content),
  };
}

```typescript
import type {
  RuleConditionEntity,
  SpendingAverageRange,
  SpendingWidget,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { calculateSpendingReportTimeRange } from '#components/reports/reportRanges';
import { normalizeSpendingAverageRange } from '#components/reports/spendingAverageRange';
import { toComparableConditions } from '#components/reports/widgetModified';

type SpendingMeta = NonNullable<SpendingWidget['meta']>;
type SpendingMode = NonNullable<SpendingMeta['mode']>;

export type SpendingWidgetSettings = Required<
  Pick<
    SpendingMeta,
    | 'conditions'
    | 'conditionsOp'
    | 'compare'
    | 'compareTo'
    | 'averageRange'
    | 'isLive'
    | 'mode'
  >
>;

/** The settings "Save" writes for a Monthly Spending widget. */
export function buildSpendingWidgetSettings({
  conditions,
  conditionsOp,
  compare,
  compareTo,
  averageRange,
  isLive,
  reportMode,
}: {
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[];
  conditionsOp: 'and' | 'or';
  compare: string;
  compareTo: string;
  averageRange: SpendingAverageRange;
  isLive: boolean;
  reportMode: SpendingMode;
}): SpendingWidgetSettings {
  return {
    conditions,
    conditionsOp,
    compare,
    compareTo,
    averageRange,
    isLive,
    mode: reportMode,
  };
}

export function toComparableSpendingSettings(
  meta: Partial<SpendingMeta> | null | undefined,
) {
  const isLive = meta?.isLive ?? true;
  const mode = meta?.mode ?? 'single-month';
  // Resolve the months the same way the report does when it opens, so a
  // widget without saved months compares equal to the defaults it shows.
  const [compare, compareTo] = calculateSpendingReportTimeRange(meta ?? {});
  return {
    ...toComparableConditions(meta?.conditions, meta?.conditionsOp),
    compare,
    // A live budget or average comparison ignores the second month.
    compareTo: isLive && mode !== 'single-month' ? undefined : compareTo,
    averageRange: normalizeSpendingAverageRange(meta?.averageRange),
    isLive,
    mode,
  };
}

import { useUpdateDashboardWidgetMutation } from '#reports/mutations';

export const defaultTimeFrame = {
  start: monthUtils.subMonths(monthUtils.currentMonth(), 120),
  end: monthUtils.subMonths(monthUtils.currentMonth(), 1),
  mode: 'full',
} satisfies TimeFrame;

// Spinner increment for the monthly contribution input, as an IntegerAmount so
// it scales with the currency: $100 at two decimal places, ¥10,000 at zero.
const CONTRIBUTION_STEP = 10000;

export function Crossover() {
  const params = useParams();
  const { data: widget, isPending } = useDashboardWidget<CrossoverWidget>({
    id: params.id,
    type: 'crossover-card',
  });

  if (isPending) {
    return <LoadingIndicator />;
  }

  return <CrossoverInner widget={widget} />;
}

type CrossoverInnerProps = { widget?: CrossoverWidget };

function CrossoverInner({ widget }: CrossoverInnerProps) {
  const locale = useLocale();
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const dispatch = useDispatch();
  const { data: accounts = [] } = useAccounts();
  const {
    data: categories = { grouped: [], list: [] },
    isPending: isCategoriesLoading,
  } = useCategories();
  const format = useFormat();

  const expenseCategoryGroups = categories.grouped.filter(
    group => !group.is_income,
  );
  const expenseCategories = categories.list.filter(c => !c.is_income);

  const [allMonths, setAllMonths] = useState<Array<{
    name: string;
    pretty: string;
  }> | null>(null);

  // Date range state
  const [start, setStart] = useState<string>('');
  const [end, setEnd] = useState<string>('');
  const [mode, setMode] = useState<TimeFrame['mode']>('static');
  const [earliestTransaction, setEarliestTransaction] = useState<string>('');
  const [latestTransaction, setLatestTransaction] = useState<string>('');

  const [selectedExpenseCategories, setSelectedExpenseCategories] =
    useState<Array<CategoryEntity>>(expenseCategories);
  const [selectedIncomeAccountIds, setSelectedIncomeAccountIds] = useState<
    string[]
  >(accounts.map(a => a.id));

  const [swr, setSwr] = useState(0.04);
  const [useCustomGrowth, setUseCustomGrowth] = useState(false);
  const [estimatedReturn, setEstimatedReturn] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [expectedContribution, setExpectedContribution] = useState<
    number | null
  >(null);
  const [projectionType, setProjectionType] = useState<
    'hampel' | 'median' | 'mean'
  >('hampel');
  const [expenseAdjustmentFactor, setExpenseAdjustmentFactor] = useState(1.0);
  const [showHiddenCategories, setShowHiddenCategories] = useState(false);
  const [selectionsInitialized, setSelectionsInitialized] = useState(false);

  // reset when widget changes
  useEffect(() => {
    setSelectionsInitialized(false);
  }, [widget?.id]);

  // initialize once when data is available
  useEffect(() => {
    if (selectionsInitialized || isCategoriesLoading) {
      return;
    }

    const initialExpenseCategories =
      widget?.meta?.expenseCategoryIds !== undefined
        ? categories.list.filter(c =>
            widget.meta!.expenseCategoryIds!.includes(c.id),
          )
        : categories.list.filter(c => !c.is_income);

    const initialIncomeAccountIds =
      widget?.meta?.incomeAccountIds !== undefined
        ? widget.meta!.incomeAccountIds!
        : accounts.map(a => a.id);

    setSelectedExpenseCategories(initialExpenseCategories);
    setSelectedIncomeAccountIds(initialIncomeAccountIds);
    setSwr(widget?.meta?.safeWithdrawalRate ?? 0.04);

    const initialEstimatedReturn = widget?.meta?.estimatedReturn ?? null;
    const initialExpectedContribution =
      widget?.meta?.expectedContribution ?? null;
    const hasCustomGrowth =
      initialEstimatedReturn != null || initialExpectedContribution != null;

    setUseCustomGrowth(hasCustomGrowth);
    setEstimatedReturn(initialEstimatedReturn);
    setExpectedContribution(initialExpectedContribution);
    setProjectionType(widget?.meta?.projectionType ?? 'hampel');
    setExpenseAdjustmentFactor(widget?.meta?.expenseAdjustmentFactor ?? 1.0);
    setShowHiddenCategories(widget?.meta?.showHiddenCategories ?? false);

    setSelectionsInitialized(true);
  }, [
    selectionsInitialized,
    accounts,
    categories.list,
    isCategoriesLoading,
    widget?.meta,
  ]);

  useEffect(() => {
    async function run() {
      const earliestTransactionData = await send('get-earliest-transaction');

      const currentMonth = monthUtils.currentMonth();
      const previousMonth = monthUtils.subMonths(currentMonth, 1);

      // Set earliest transaction date
      const earliestDate = earliestTransactionData
        ? earliestTransactionData.date
        : monthUtils.firstDayOfMonth(previousMonth);
      setEarliestTransaction(earliestDate);

      // Set latest transaction date, ensuring it doesn't include current month
      const latestDate = monthUtils.lastDayOfMonth(previousMonth);
      setLatestTransaction(latestDate);

      const allMonths = monthUtils
        .rangeInclusive(earliestDate, latestDate)
        .map(month => ({
          name: month,
          pretty: monthUtils.format(month, 'MMMM yyyy', locale),
        }))
        .reverse();

      setAllMonths(allMonths);
    }
    void run();
  }, [locale]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (latestTransaction && allMonths?.length) {
      const [initialStart, initialEnd, mode] = calculateTimeRange(
        widget?.meta?.timeFrame,
        defaultTimeFrame,
        latestTransaction,
      );
      const earliestMonth = allMonths[allMonths.length - 1].name;
      const latestMonth = allMonths[0].name;
      let start = initialStart;
      let end = initialEnd;

      const clampMonth = (m: string) => {
        if (monthUtils.isBefore(m, earliestMonth)) return earliestMonth;
        if (monthUtils.isAfter(m, latestMonth)) return latestMonth;
        return m;
      };

      // For both sliding-window and full modes, ensure end doesn't include current month
      if (mode === 'sliding-window') {
        // Shift both start and end back one month for sliding-window
        start = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(start, 1));
        end = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(end, 1));
      } else if (mode === 'full') {
        start = earliestMonth;
        end = latestMonth;
      } else {
        start = clampMonth(start);
        end = clampMonth(end);
      }
      if (monthUtils.isBefore(end, start)) {
        end = start;
      }
      setStart(start);
      setEnd(end);
      setMode(mode);
    }
  }, [latestTransaction, widget?.meta?.timeFrame, allMonths]);

  function onChangeDates(start: string, end: string, mode: TimeFrame['mode']) {
    if (!allMonths?.length) {
      return;
    }
    const earliestMonth = allMonths[allMonths.length - 1].name;
    const latestMonth = allMonths[0].name;

    const clampMonth = (m: string) => {
      if (monthUtils.isBefore(m, earliestMonth)) return earliestMonth;
      if (monthUtils.isAfter(m, latestMonth)) return latestMonth;
      return m;
    };

    // For both sliding-window and full modes, ensure end doesn't include current month
    if (mode === 'sliding-window') {
      // Shift both start and end back one month for sliding-window
      start = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(start, 1));
      end = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(end, 1));
    } else if (mode === 'full') {
      start = earliestMonth;
      end = latestMonth;
    } else {
      start = clampMonth(start);
      end = clampMonth(end);
    }
    if (monthUtils.isBefore(end, start)) {
      end = start;
    }
    setStart(start);
    setEnd(end);
    setMode(mode);
  }

  const updateDashboardWidgetMutation = useUpdateDashboardWidgetMutation();

  async function onSaveWidget() {
    if (!widget) {
      dispatch(
        addNotification({
          notification: {
            type: 'error',
            message: t('Save failed: No widget found to save.'),
          },
        }),
      );
      return;
    }

    updateDashboardWidgetMutation.mutate(
      {
        widget: {
          id: widget.id,
          meta: {
            ...(widget.meta ?? {}),
            expenseCategoryIds: selectedExpenseCategories.map(c => c.id),
            incomeAccountIds: selectedIncomeAccountIds,
            safeWithdrawalRate: swr,
            estimatedReturn: useCustomGrowth ? (estimatedReturn ?? 0) : null,
            expectedContribution: useCustomGrowth
              ? (expectedContribution ?? 0)
              : null,
            projectionType,
            expenseAdjustmentFactor,
            showHiddenCategories,
            timeFrame: { start, end, mode },
          },
        },
      },
      {
        onSuccess: () => {
          dispatch(
            addNotification({
              notification: {
                type: 'message',
                message: t('Dashboard widget successfully saved.'),
              },
            }),
          );
        },
      },
    );
  }

  // Memoize the derived values to avoid recreating them on every render
  const expenseCategoryIds = useMemo(
    () =>
      selectedExpenseCategories
        .filter(c => showHiddenCategories || !c.hidden)
```

```typescript
import * as monthUtils from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
import type {
  AccountEntity,
  CategoryEntity,
  CrossoverWidget,
  TimeFrame,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { calculateTimeRange } from '#components/reports/reportRanges';
import { toComparableTimeFrame } from '#components/reports/widgetModified';

type CrossoverMeta = NonNullable<CrossoverWidget['meta']>;

export const defaultTimeFrame = {
  start: monthUtils.subMonths(monthUtils.currentMonth(), 120),
  end: monthUtils.subMonths(monthUtils.currentMonth(), 1),
  mode: 'full',
} satisfies TimeFrame;

/**
 * Fits a range to the months the report can show. The current month is never
 * included, so sliding windows end last month and "all time" spans every
 * month with data.
 */
export function adjustCrossoverRange(
  start: string,
  end: string,
  mode: TimeFrame['mode'],
  earliestMonth: string,
  latestMonth: string,
): [string, string] {
  const clampMonth = (month: string) => {
    if (monthUtils.isBefore(month, earliestMonth)) return earliestMonth;
    if (monthUtils.isAfter(month, latestMonth)) return latestMonth;
    return month;
  };

  let adjustedStart: string;
  let adjustedEnd: string;
  if (mode === 'sliding-window') {
    adjustedStart = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(start, 1));
    adjustedEnd = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(end, 1));
  } else if (mode === 'full') {
    adjustedStart = earliestMonth;
    adjustedEnd = latestMonth;
  } else {
    adjustedStart = clampMonth(start);
    adjustedEnd = clampMonth(end);
  }
  if (monthUtils.isBefore(adjustedEnd, adjustedStart)) {
    adjustedEnd = adjustedStart;
  }
  return [adjustedStart, adjustedEnd];
}

export type CrossoverRangeContext = {
  earliestMonth: string;
  latestMonth: string;
  latestTransaction: string;
};

/** The range the report shows for a saved time frame. */
export function resolveCrossoverTimeFrame(
  timeFrame: Partial<TimeFrame> | undefined,
  { earliestMonth, latestMonth, latestTransaction }: CrossoverRangeContext,
): TimeFrame {
  const [start, end, mode] = calculateTimeRange(
    timeFrame,
    defaultTimeFrame,
    latestTransaction,
  );
  const [adjustedStart, adjustedEnd] = adjustCrossoverRange(
    start,
    end,
    mode,
    earliestMonth,
    latestMonth,
  );
  return { start: adjustedStart, end: adjustedEnd, mode };
}

export type CrossoverWidgetSettings = Required<
  Pick<
    CrossoverMeta,
    | 'expenseCategoryIds'
    | 'incomeAccountIds'
    | 'safeWithdrawalRate'
    | 'estimatedReturn'
    | 'expectedContribution'
    | 'projectionType'
    | 'expenseAdjustmentFactor'
    | 'showHiddenCategories'
    | 'timeFrame'
  >
>;

/** The settings "Save widget" writes for a Crossover Point widget. */
export function buildCrossoverWidgetSettings({
  selectedExpenseCategories,
  selectedIncomeAccountIds,
  swr,
  useCustomGrowth,
  estimatedReturn,
  expectedContribution,
  projectionType,
  expenseAdjustmentFactor,
  showHiddenCategories,
  start,
  end,
  mode,
}: {
  selectedExpenseCategories: Array<Pick<CategoryEntity, 'id'>>;
  selectedIncomeAccountIds: string[];
  swr: number;
  useCustomGrowth: boolean;
  estimatedReturn: number | null;
  expectedContribution: number | null;
  projectionType: 'hampel' | 'median' | 'mean';
  expenseAdjustmentFactor: number;
  showHiddenCategories: boolean;
  start: string;
  end: string;
  mode: TimeFrame['mode'];
}): CrossoverWidgetSettings {
  return {
    expenseCategoryIds: selectedExpenseCategories.map(c => c.id),
    incomeAccountIds: selectedIncomeAccountIds,
    safeWithdrawalRate: swr,
    estimatedReturn: useCustomGrowth ? (estimatedReturn ?? 0) : null,
    expectedContribution: useCustomGrowth ? (expectedContribution ?? 0) : null,
    projectionType,
    expenseAdjustmentFactor,
    showHiddenCategories,
    timeFrame: { start, end, mode },
  };
}

export type CrossoverComparisonContext = {
  categories: Array<Pick<CategoryEntity, 'id' | 'is_income'>>;
  accounts: Array<Pick<AccountEntity, 'id'>>;
  /** Missing until the months with data have loaded. */
  range?: CrossoverRangeContext;
};

export function toComparableCrossoverSettings(
  meta: Partial<CrossoverMeta> | null | undefined,
  { categories, accounts, range }: CrossoverComparisonContext,
) {
  // Mirrors how the report reads the saved selections: no saved list means
  // everything, and categories that no longer exist are dropped.
  const expenseCategoryIds =
    meta?.expenseCategoryIds !== undefined
      ? categories
          .filter(c => meta.expenseCategoryIds?.includes(c.id))
          .map(c => c.id)
      : categories.filter(c => !c.is_income).map(c => c.id);
  const incomeAccountIds = meta?.incomeAccountIds ?? accounts.map(a => a.id);

  return {
    expenseCategoryIds: [...expenseCategoryIds].sort(),
    incomeAccountIds: [...incomeAccountIds].sort(),
    safeWithdrawalRate: meta?.safeWithdrawalRate ?? 0.04,
    estimatedReturn: meta?.estimatedReturn ?? null,
    expectedContribution: meta?.expectedContribution ?? null,
    projectionType: meta?.projectionType ?? 'hampel',
    expenseAdjustmentFactor: meta?.expenseAdjustmentFactor ?? 1.0,
    showHiddenCategories: meta?.showHiddenCategories ?? false,
    timeFrame: toComparableTimeFrame(
      range
        ? resolveCrossoverTimeFrame(meta?.timeFrame, range)
        : meta?.timeFrame,
      defaultTimeFrame,
    ),
  };
}

import type { RuleConditionEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { calculateTimeRange } from './reportRanges';
import {
  isWidgetModified,
  toComparableConditions,
  toComparableTimeFrame,
} from './widgetModified';

// In test mode, monthUtils.currentMonth() returns '2017-01'.
describe('toComparableTimeFrame', () => {
  it('compares a static range by its dates', () => {
    expect(
      toComparableTimeFrame({
        start: '2016-03',
        end: '2016-05',
        mode: 'static',
      }),
    ).toEqual({ mode: 'static', start: '2016-03', end: '2016-05' });
  });

  it('compares a month sliding window by its width, not its dates', () => {
    const savedLastYear = toComparableTimeFrame({
      start: '2015-08',
      end: '2016-01',
      mode: 'sliding-window',
    });
    const [start, end, mode] = calculateTimeRange({
      start: '2015-08',
      end: '2016-01',
      mode: 'sliding-window',
    });

    expect(savedLastYear).toEqual({
      mode: 'sliding-window',
      shape: 'month',
      width: 5,
    });
    expect(toComparableTimeFrame({ start, end, mode })).toEqual(savedLastYear);
  });

  it('compares a day sliding window by its width in days', () => {
    expect(
      toComparableTimeFrame({
        start: '2016-12-01',
        end: '2016-12-31',
        mode: 'sliding-window',
      }),
    ).toEqual({ mode: 'sliding-window', shape: 'day', width: 30 });
  });

  it('tells month and day sliding windows apart', () => {
    expect(
      toComparableTimeFrame({
        start: '2016-12',
        end: '2017-01',
        mode: 'sliding-window',
      }),
    ).not.toEqual(
      toComparableTimeFrame({
        start: '2016-12-01',
        end: '2017-01-01',
        mode: 'sliding-window',
      }),
    );
  });

  it.each([
    'full',
    'lastMonth',
    'lastYear',
    'yearToDate',
    'priorYearToDate',
    'currentQuarter',
    'previousQuarter',
  ] as const)('compares a %s range by its mode only', mode => {
    expect(
      toComparableTimeFrame({ start: '2014-01', end: '2014-02', mode }),
    ).toEqual(
      toComparableTimeFrame({ start: '2016-06', end: '2017-01', mode }),
    );
  });

  it('uses the default time frame when none is saved', () => {
    expect(toComparableTimeFrame(undefined, { mode: 'full' })).toEqual({
      mode: 'full',
    });
    // Same fallback as calculateTimeRange: a six-month sliding window.
    expect(toComparableTimeFrame(undefined)).toEqual({
      mode: 'sliding-window',
      shape: 'month',
      width: 5,
    });
  });
});

describe('toComparableConditions', () => {
  it('treats missing conditions as no filters joined with "and"', () => {
    expect(toComparableConditions(undefined, undefined)).toEqual({
      conditions: [],
      conditionsOp: 'and',
    });
  });
});

describe('isWidgetModified', () => {
  const condition = {
    field: 'amount',
    op: 'gt',
    value: 100,
  } as RuleConditionEntity;

  it('is false without a widget', () => {
    expect(
      isWidgetModified({
        hasWidget: false,
        isReady: true,
        saved: { a: 1 },
        current: { a: 2 },
      }),
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it('is false until the report is ready', () => {
    expect(
      isWidgetModified({
        hasWidget: true,
        isReady: false,
        saved: { a: 1 },
        current: { a: 2 },
      }),
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it('is true when a setting differs', () => {
    expect(
      isWidgetModified({
        hasWidget: true,
        isReady: true,
        saved: { conditions: [] },
        current: { conditions: [condition] },
      }),
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  it('ignores keys that are undefined, as saving does', () => {
    expect(
      isWidgetModified({
        hasWidget: true,
        isReady: true,
        saved: { conditions: [{ ...condition }] },
        current: { conditions: [{ ...condition, options: undefined }] },
      }),
    ).toBe(false);
  });
});

import type {
  NetWorthWidget,
  RuleConditionEntity,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { isWidgetModified } from '#components/reports/widgetModified';

import {
  buildNetWorthWidgetSettings,
  toComparableNetWorthSettings,
} from './netWorthWidgetSettings';
import type { NetWorthWidgetSettings } from './netWorthWidgetSettings';

type Meta = NonNullable<NetWorthWidget['meta']>;

const CONDITION = {
  field: 'account',
  op: 'is',
  value: 'acct-1',
} as RuleConditionEntity;

const SAVED_META: Meta = {
  name: 'My net worth',
  conditions: [CONDITION],
  conditionsOp: 'or',
  interval: 'Yearly',
  mode: 'stacked',
  timeFrame: { start: '2016-01', end: '2016-06', mode: 'static' },
};

// What the report holds after opening SAVED_META.
const UNCHANGED = buildNetWorthWidgetSettings({
  conditions: [CONDITION],
  conditionsOp: 'or',
  interval: 'Yearly',
  graphMode: 'stacked',
  start: '2016-01',
  end: '2016-06',
  mode: 'static',
});

// One different value for every setting "Save widget" writes.
const CHANGES: { [K in keyof NetWorthWidgetSettings]: NetWorthWidgetSettings[K] } =
  {
    conditions: [],
    conditionsOp: 'and',
    interval: 'Monthly',
    mode: 'trend',
    timeFrame: { start: '2016-01', end: '2016-07', mode: 'static' },
  };

function isModified(saved: Partial<Meta> | null, current: Partial<Meta>) {
  return isWidgetModified({
    hasWidget: true,
    isReady: true,
    saved: toComparableNetWorthSettings(saved),
    current: toComparableNetWorthSettings(current),
  });
}

describe('Net Worth widget settings', () => {
  it('checks exactly the settings "Save widget" writes', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(UNCHANGED).sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(CHANGES).sort());
  });

  it('is unchanged right after opening the widget', () => {
    expect(isModified(SAVED_META, UNCHANGED)).toBe(false);
  });

  it.each(Object.keys(CHANGES) as Array<keyof NetWorthWidgetSettings>)(
    'notices a change to %s',
    key => {
      expect(isModified(SAVED_META, { ...UNCHANGED, [key]: CHANGES[key] })).toBe(
        true,
      );
    },
  );

  it('ignores the name, which is saved separately', () => {
    expect(isModified({ ...SAVED_META, name: 'Renamed' }, UNCHANGED)).toBe(
      false,
    );
  });

  it('matches the defaults when nothing is saved', () => {
    const defaults = buildNetWorthWidgetSettings({
      conditions: [],
      conditionsOp: 'and',
      interval: 'Monthly',
      graphMode: 'trend',
      start: '2016-08',
      end: '2017-01',
      mode: 'sliding-window',
    });
    expect(isModified(null, defaults)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('defaults to a weekly interval for last month', () => {
    const lastMonth = buildNetWorthWidgetSettings({
      conditions: [],
      conditionsOp: 'and',
      interval: 'Weekly',
      graphMode: 'trend',
      start: '2016-12',
      end: '2016-12',
      mode: 'lastMonth',
    });
    expect(
      isModified(
        { timeFrame: { start: '2016-11', end: '2016-11', mode: 'lastMonth' } },
        lastMonth,
      ),
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it('does not flag a sliding window saved in an earlier month', () => {
    const reopened = buildNetWorthWidgetSettings({
      ...{ conditions: [], conditionsOp: 'and' as const },
      interval: 'Monthly',
      graphMode: 'trend',
      start: '2016-08',
      end: '2017-01',
      mode: 'sliding-window',
    });
    expect(
      isModified(
        {
          timeFrame: { start: '2016-02', end: '2016-07', mode: 'sliding-window' },
        },
        reopened,
      ),
    ).toBe(false);
  });
});

import type {
  RuleConditionEntity,
  SpendingWidget,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { calculateSpendingReportTimeRange } from '#components/reports/reportRanges';
import { DEFAULT_SPENDING_AVERAGE_RANGE } from '#components/reports/spendingAverageRange';
import { isWidgetModified } from '#components/reports/widgetModified';

import {
  buildSpendingWidgetSettings,
  toComparableSpendingSettings,
} from './spendingWidgetSettings';
import type { SpendingWidgetSettings } from './spendingWidgetSettings';

type Meta = NonNullable<SpendingWidget['meta']>;

const CONDITION = {
  field: 'category',
  op: 'is',
  value: 'cat-1',
} as RuleConditionEntity;

const SAVED_META: Meta = {
  name: 'My spending',
  conditions: [CONDITION],
  conditionsOp: 'or',
  compare: '2016-06',
  compareTo: '2016-03',
  averageRange: { mode: 'last-n-months', months: 6 },
  isLive: false,
  mode: 'single-month',
};

// What the report holds after opening SAVED_META.
const UNCHANGED = buildSpendingWidgetSettings({
  conditions: [CONDITION],
  conditionsOp: 'or',
  compare: '2016-06',
  compareTo: '2016-03',
  averageRange: { mode: 'last-n-months', months: 6 },
  isLive: false,
  reportMode: 'single-month',
});

// One different value for every setting "Save" writes.
const CHANGES: { [K in keyof SpendingWidgetSettings]: SpendingWidgetSettings[K] } =
  {
    conditions: [],
    conditionsOp: 'and',
    compare: '2016-07',
    compareTo: '2016-02',
    averageRange: { mode: 'year-to-date' },
    isLive: true,
    mode: 'budget',
  };

function isModified(saved: Partial<Meta> | null, current: Partial<Meta>) {
  return isWidgetModified({
    hasWidget: true,
    isReady: true,
    saved: toComparableSpendingSettings(saved),
    current: toComparableSpendingSettings(current),
  });
}

function openedState(meta: Partial<Meta>) {
  // Mirrors how the report fills its state from a saved widget.
  const [compare, compareTo] = calculateSpendingReportTimeRange(meta);
  return buildSpendingWidgetSettings({
    conditions: meta.conditions ?? [],
    conditionsOp: meta.conditionsOp ?? 'and',
    compare,
    compareTo,
    averageRange: meta.averageRange ?? DEFAULT_SPENDING_AVERAGE_RANGE,
    isLive: meta.isLive ?? true,
    reportMode: meta.mode ?? 'single-month',
  });
}

describe('Spending widget settings', () => {
  it('checks exactly the settings "Save" writes', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(UNCHANGED).sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(CHANGES).sort());
  });

  it('is unchanged right after opening the widget', () => {
    expect(isModified(SAVED_META, UNCHANGED)).toBe(false);
    expect(isModified(SAVED_META, openedState(SAVED_META))).toBe(false);
  });

  it.each(Object.keys(CHANGES) as Array<keyof SpendingWidgetSettings>)(
    'notices a change to %s',
    key => {
      expect(
        isModified(SAVED_META, { ...UNCHANGED, [key]: CHANGES[key] }),
      ).toBe(true);
    },
  );

  it('ignores the name, which is saved separately', () => {
    expect(isModified({ ...SAVED_META, name: 'Renamed' }, UNCHANGED)).toBe(
      false,
    );
  });

  it('matches the defaults when nothing is saved', () => {
    expect(isModified(null, openedState({}))).toBe(false);
  });

  it('compares a live budget comparison by its first month only', () => {
    const saved: Partial<Meta> = {
      compare: '2016-06',
      compareTo: '2016-05',
      isLive: true,
      mode: 'budget',
    };
    // Opening a live budget comparison sets both months to the first one.
    expect(isModified(saved, openedState(saved))).toBe(false);
  });

  it('treats an unsupported average range as the default', () => {
    expect(
      isModified(
        {
          ...SAVED_META,
          averageRange: { mode: 'last-n-months', months: 5 as 6 },
        },
        { ...UNCHANGED, averageRange: DEFAULT_SPENDING_AVERAGE_RANGE },
      ),
    ).toBe(false);
  });
});

  it.each(Object.keys(CHANGES) as Array<keyof CrossoverWidgetSettings>)(
    'notices a change to %s',
    key => {
      expect(
        isModified(SAVED_META, { ...UNCHANGED, [key]: CHANGES[key] }),
      ).toBe(true);
    },
  );

  it('notices turning custom growth off', () => {
    const withoutGrowth = buildCrossoverWidgetSettings({
      selectedExpenseCategories: [{ id: 'food' }, { id: 'rent' }],
      selectedIncomeAccountIds: ['savings'],
      swr: 0.035,
      useCustomGrowth: false,
      estimatedReturn: 0.05,
      expectedContribution: 100000,
      projectionType: 'median',
      expenseAdjustmentFactor: 1.2,
      showHiddenCategories: true,
      start: '2015-01',
      end: '2016-06',
      mode: 'static',
    });
    expect(isModified(SAVED_META, withoutGrowth)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('ignores the name, which is saved separately', () => {
    expect(isModified({ ...SAVED_META, name: 'Renamed' }, UNCHANGED)).toBe(
      false,
    );
  });

  it('ignores saved categories that no longer exist', () => {
    expect(
      isModified(
        { ...SAVED_META, expenseCategoryIds: ['food', 'rent', 'deleted'] },
        UNCHANGED,
      ),
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it('matches the defaults when nothing is saved', () => {
    if (!CONTEXT.range) throw new Error('missing range');
    const { start, end, mode } = resolveCrossoverTimeFrame(
      undefined,
      CONTEXT.range,
    );
    const defaults = buildCrossoverWidgetSettings({
      selectedExpenseCategories: [{ id: 'food' }, { id: 'rent' }],
      selectedIncomeAccountIds: ['checking', 'savings'],
      swr: 0.04,
      useCustomGrowth: false,
      estimatedReturn: null,

      projectionType: 'hampel',
      expenseAdjustmentFactor: 1,
      showHiddenCategories: false,
      start,
      end,
      mode,
    });
    expect(isModified(null, defaults)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('does not flag a sliding window the report moved back a month', () => {
    if (!CONTEXT.range) throw new Error('missing range');
    const savedTimeFrame = {
      start: '2015-07',
      end: '2016-06',
      mode: 'sliding-window' as const,
    };
    const opened = resolveCrossoverTimeFrame(savedTimeFrame, CONTEXT.range);
    expect(opened).toEqual({
      start: '2016-01',
      end: '2016-12',
      mode: 'sliding-window',
    });
    expect(
      isModified(
        { ...SAVED_META, timeFrame: savedTimeFrame },
        { ...UNCHANGED, timeFrame: opened },
      ),
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it('does not flag a range the report clamped to the months with data', () => {
    if (!CONTEXT.range) throw new Error('missing range');
    const savedTimeFrame = {
      start: '2010-01',
      end: '2016-06',
      mode: 'static' as const,
    };
    const opened = resolveCrossoverTimeFrame(savedTimeFrame, CONTEXT.range);
    expect(opened.start).toBe('2014-01');
    expect(
      isModified(
        { ...SAVED_META, timeFrame: savedTimeFrame },
        { ...UNCHANGED, timeFrame: opened },
      ),
    ).toBe(false);
  });

// Minimal connection mock used by desktop-client component tests.
//
// This mirrors `@actual-app/core`'s test-only mock implementation so that
// `useSpreadsheet()` and other code paths can call `send()` and receive a
// promise with a stable shape.

type Listener = (args: unknown) => void;
type Handler = (args: unknown) => unknown | Promise<unknown>;

let listeners = new Map<string, Array<Listener>>();
let serverHandler:
  | null
  | ((msg: { name: string; args: unknown; catchErrors: boolean }) => unknown) =
  null;

export const initServer = (handlers: Record<string, Handler>) => {
  serverHandler = msg => {
    const { name, args, catchErrors } = msg;
    if (handlers[name]) {
      return Promise.resolve().then(() => {
        const promise = Promise.resolve(handlers[name](args));

        if (catchErrors) {
          return promise.then(
            data => ({ data }),
            error => ({ error }),
          );
        }

        return promise;
      });
    }
  };
};

export const clearServer = async () => {
  serverHandler = null;
  listeners = new Map();
};

export const serverPush = (name: string, args: unknown) => {
  void Promise.resolve().then(() => {
    const listens = listeners.get(name);
    if (listens) {
      listens.forEach(listener => {
        listener(args);
      });
    }
  });
};

export const send = async (
  name: string,
  args: unknown,
  { catchErrors = false } = {},
) => {
  if (serverHandler) {
    return serverHandler({ name, args, catchErrors });
  } else {
    throw new Error('`send` called with no mock server installed');
```

export const sendCatch = (name: string, args: unknown) => {
  return send(name, args, { catchErrors: true });
};

export const listen = (name: string, cb: Listener) => {
  if (!listeners.get(name)) {
    listeners.set(name, []);
  }

  listeners.get(name)!.push(cb);

  return () => {
    const arr = listeners.get(name) ?? [];
    listeners.set(
      name,
      arr.filter(cb_ => cb_ !== cb),
    );
  };
};

} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

}));

}));

const SAVED_TIME_FRAME: TimeFrame = {
  start: '2024-01',
  end: '2024-06',
  mode: 'static',
};
const ACCOUNT_FILTER: RuleConditionEntity = {
  field: 'account',
  op: 'is',
  value: 'acct-1',
  type: 'id',
};

// The real Header pulls in the filter menus and date pickers. This stub lets
// tests change the date range, put it back, and add a filter.
vi.mock('#components/reports/Header', () => ({
  Header: ({
    start,
    end,
    mode,
    onChangeDates,
    onApply,
    children,
  }: {
    start: string;
    end: string;
    mode: TimeFrame['mode'];
    onChangeDates: (start: string, end: string, mode: TimeFrame['mode']) => void;
    onApply: (condition: RuleConditionEntity) => void;
    children?: ReactNode;
  }) => (
    <div>
      <span data-testid="header-range">{`${start} ${end} ${mode}`}</span>
      <button onClick={() => onChangeDates('2024-03', '2024-06', 'static')}>
        Change dates
      </button>
      <button onClick={() => onChangeDates('2024-01', '2024-06', 'static')}>
        Restore dates
      </button>
      <button
        onClick={() =>
          onApply({
            field: 'account',
            op: 'is',
            value: 'acct-1',
            type: 'id',
          })
        }
      >
        Add filter
      </button>
      {children}
    </div>
  ),
}));

const WIDGET_ID = 'net-worth-widget-1';

function makeWidget(meta: NetWorthWidget['meta']): NetWorthWidget {
  return {
    id: WIDGET_ID,
    dashboard_page_id: 'page-1',
    type: 'net-worth-card',
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    width: 4,
    height: 2,
    meta,
    tombstone: false,
  };
}

function renderNetWorth({
  path = `/reports/net-worth/${WIDGET_ID}`,
}: { path?: string } = {}) {
  let widgets = [
    makeWidget({ name: 'My net worth', timeFrame: SAVED_TIME_FRAME }),
  ];
  const updateWidget = vi.fn(async (update: unknown) => {
    const { id, meta } = update as Pick<NetWorthWidget, 'id' | 'meta'>;
    widgets = widgets.map(widget =>
      widget.id === id ? { ...widget, meta } : widget,
    );
  });
  initServer({
    query: () => Promise.resolve({ data: widgets, dependencies: [] }),
    'get-earliest-transaction': async () => ({ date: '2023-01-05' }),
    'get-latest-transaction': async () => ({ date: '2024-06-20' }),
    'dashboard-update-widget': updateWidget,
  });
  const queryClient = createTestQueryClient();
  const store = configureTestAppStore({ queryClient });

  render(
    <TestProviders queryClient={queryClient} store={store}>
      <MemoryRouter initialEntries={[path]}>
        <Routes>
          <Route path="/reports/net-worth" element={<NetWorth />} />
          <Route path="/reports/net-worth/:id" element={<NetWorth />} />
        </Routes>
      </MemoryRouter>
    </TestProviders>,
  );

  return { updateWidget };
}

async function waitForSavedRange() {
  await waitFor(() =>
    expect(screen.getByTestId('header-range')).toHaveTextContent(
      '2024-01 2024-06 static',
    ),
  );
}

describe('NetWorth', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    vi.mocked(useNavigate).mockReturnValue(vi.fn());
    vi.mocked(useReport).mockReturnValue({
      netWorth: 0,
      totalChange: 0,
      totalChangePercent: 0,
      graphData: { data: [], hasNegative: false, start: '', end: '' },
      accounts: [],
    });
    (useResponsive as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue({
      isNarrowWidth: false,
    });
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await clearServer();
  });

  it('shows "(modified)" only while the settings differ from the saved widget', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { updateWidget } = renderNetWorth();
    await waitForSavedRange();
    expect(screen.queryByText('(modified)')).not.toBeInTheDocument();

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Change dates' }));
    expect(screen.getByText('(modified)')).toBeInTheDocument();

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Restore dates' }));
    expect(screen.queryByText('(modified)')).not.toBeInTheDocument();

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add filter' }));
    expect(screen.getByText('(modified)')).toBeInTheDocument();

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save widget' }));
    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(updateWidget).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        id: WIDGET_ID,
        meta: {
          name: 'My net worth',
          conditions: [ACCOUNT_FILTER],
          conditionsOp: 'and',
          interval: 'Monthly',
          mode: 'trend',
          timeFrame: SAVED_TIME_FRAME,
        },
      }),
    );
    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(screen.queryByText('(modified)')).not.toBeInTheDocument(),
    );
  });

  it('shows the label in the mobile header too', async () => {
    (useResponsive as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue({
      isNarrowWidth: true,
    });
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderNetWorth();
    await waitForSavedRange();

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Change dates' }));

    expect(screen.getByText('(modified)')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('never shows the label without a widget', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderNetWorth({ path: '/reports/net-worth' });
    await screen.findByTestId('header-range');

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Change dates' }));

    expect(screen.queryByText('(modified)')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(
      screen.queryByRole('button', { name: 'Save widget' }),
    ).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-08 21:18:15Z)**_

The "(modified)" label now works on all eight reports, and typecheck, lint and the report tests (41 files, 676 tests) pass. I haven't run the app to check it by hand. Nothing is committed yet; everything is on a new branch, `feat/issue-125-modified-label`.

**How it works**
- **One function per report:** each report has a settings function that builds what Save widget writes, and the same output is used for the comparison. So the label can only react to settings that Save widget actually saves. The baseline is the saved widget itself: a successful save refreshes it and the label disappears, a failed save leaves it and the label stays.
- **The label:** a shared [ReportWidgetTitle.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/ReportWidgetTitle.tsx) puts the title and label in both the desktop and mobile headers. Custom Reports now use the same [ModifiedLabel.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/ModifiedLabel.tsx), so the wording matches.
- **No flash on load:** each page waits until its saved settings have loaded before comparing.

**Your decisions, as built**
- **Date ranges:** relative ranges compare the setting, not the dates. A sliding window compares its length, "all time" and the named ranges compare only the mode, and a fixed range compares its exact dates. A widget saved as "last 6 months" won't show modified next month.
- **Calendar:** clicking a day or month on the card counts as a change, because Save widget would store that date filter.
- **Summary:** renaming now saves only the name, like the other seven reports.
- **Save widget** stays enabled.

**Things I did that weren't spelled out in the plan**
- **Crossover:** on load it shifts sliding windows back a month and fits ranges to the months that have data. I moved that adjustment into its settings module so the page and the comparison share it. Without that, the label showed right after opening.
- **Summary display setting:** the divisor settings only count when "Show as" is Percentage, because the report resets the divisor filters when it opens with any other choice.
- **Imports:** Cash Flow's and Crossover's default date ranges moved into their settings modules, and their dashboard cards now import from there. I also added one entry to the import map in `packages/desktop-client/package.json` for the shared helper.

**Tests**
- **Every report:** each has a test that pins the exact list of settings Save widget writes, checks that changing each one shows the label, and checks that changing the name does not.
- **Goal page:** new tests cover label shown, cleared after a successful save, kept after a failed save, not shown for a rename alone, and never shown without a widget.
- **Net Worth page:** a new `NetWorth.test.tsx` walks through the issue's user scenario step by step, plus the mobile header.

**Watch out:** running `yarn lint:fix` across the whole repo on your Windows checkout converted about 500 unrelated files to Unix line endings. Only line endings changed in them, and I restored them all. To avoid it, format only the changed files. I saved a memory about this.

**Problems I found but didn't fix**
- Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover and Calendar may get stuck on the loading spinner when opened without a widget (for example `/reports/cash-flow`). I haven't run this to confirm. The label is unaffected either way.
- Calendar shows two error messages when a save fails.

I also added a release note in `upcoming-release-notes/report-widget-modified-label.md`, credited to `bennettmatuszewski`.

Next step is checking it by hand in the demo budget (`yarn start`, then "View demo"). After that I can commit and open the PR with the `[AI]` title prefix.

export function toComparableSpendingSettings(
  meta: Partial<SpendingMeta> | null | undefined,
) {
  const isLive = meta?.isLive ?? true;
  const mode = meta?.mode ?? 'single-month';
  // Resolve the months the same way the report does when it opens, so a
  // widget without saved months compares equal to the defaults it shows.
  const [compare, compareTo] = calculateSpendingReportTimeRange(meta ?? {});
  return {
    ...toComparableConditions(meta?.conditions, meta?.conditionsOp),
    compare,
    // A live budget or average comparison ignores the second month.
    compareTo: isLive && mode !== 'single-month' ? undefined : compareTo,
    averageRange: normalizeSpendingAverageRange(meta?.averageRange),
    isLive,
    mode,
  };

const DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT: SummaryContent = {
  type: 'sum',
  divisorAllTimeDateRange: false,
  divisorConditions: [],
  divisorConditionsOp: 'and',
} as SummaryContent;

/** Reads the saved "Show as" settings, falling back to a plain sum. */
export function parseSummaryContent(content?: string): SummaryContent {
  if (!content) {
    return DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT;
  }
  try {
    return JSON.parse(content);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to parse widget meta content:', error);
    return DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT;
  }
}

  };

function toComparableSummaryContent(content?: string) {
  const parsed = parseSummaryContent(content);
  if (parsed.type !== 'percentage') {
    // The divisor settings only apply to percentages, and the report resets
    // the divisor filters when it opens with any other type.
    return { type: parsed.type ?? 'sum', fontSize: parsed.fontSize };
  }
  const divisor = toComparableConditions(
    parsed.divisorConditions,
    parsed.divisorConditionsOp,
  );
  return {
    type: parsed.type,
    fontSize: parsed.fontSize,
    divisorConditions: divisor.conditions,
    divisorConditionsOp: divisor.conditionsOp,
    divisorAllTimeDateRange: parsed.divisorAllTimeDateRange ?? false,
  };
}

---- crossover
type CrossoverMeta = NonNullable<CrossoverWidget['meta']>;

export const defaultTimeFrame = {
  start: monthUtils.subMonths(monthUtils.currentMonth(), 120),
  end: monthUtils.subMonths(monthUtils.currentMonth(), 1),
  mode: 'full',
} satisfies TimeFrame;

/**
 * Fits a range to the months the report can show. The current month is never
 * included, so sliding windows end last month and "all time" spans every
 * month with data.
 */
export function adjustCrossoverRange(
  start: string,
  end: string,
  mode: TimeFrame['mode'],
  earliestMonth: string,
  latestMonth: string,
): [string, string] {
  const clampMonth = (month: string) => {
    if (monthUtils.isBefore(month, earliestMonth)) return earliestMonth;
    if (monthUtils.isAfter(month, latestMonth)) return latestMonth;
    return month;
  };

  let adjustedStart: string;
  let adjustedEnd: string;
  if (mode === 'sliding-window') {
    adjustedStart = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(start, 1));
    adjustedEnd = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(end, 1));
  } else if (mode === 'full') {
    adjustedStart = earliestMonth;
    adjustedEnd = latestMonth;
  } else {
    adjustedStart = clampMonth(start);
    adjustedEnd = clampMonth(end);
  }
  if (monthUtils.isBefore(adjustedEnd, adjustedStart)) {
    adjustedEnd = adjustedStart;
  }
  return [adjustedStart, adjustedEnd];
}

export function toComparableCrossoverSettings(
  meta: Partial<CrossoverMeta> | null | undefined,
  { categories, accounts, range }: CrossoverComparisonContext,
) {
  // Mirrors how the report reads the saved selections: no saved list means
  // everything, and categories that no longer exist are dropped.
  const expenseCategoryIds =
    meta?.expenseCategoryIds !== undefined
      ? categories
          .filter(c => meta.expenseCategoryIds?.includes(c.id))
          .map(c => c.id)
      : categories.filter(c => !c.is_income).map(c => c.id);
  const incomeAccountIds = meta?.incomeAccountIds ?? accounts.map(a => a.id);

  return {
    expenseCategoryIds: [...expenseCategoryIds].sort(),
    incomeAccountIds: [...incomeAccountIds].sort(),
    safeWithdrawalRate: meta?.safeWithdrawalRate ?? 0.04,

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.

## Description

Closes #125

## Testing

- 新增 9 个单元测试文件（共享工具 + 8 个报表各一个）。每个报表的测试都会锁定 "Save widget" 写入的设置列表，逐一验证每项设置的修改都会显示标签，并验证修改名称不会显示标签。
- 页面测试：
  - Goal（扩展现有测试）：标签显示；保存成功后消失；保存失败时保留；仅重命名不显示；没有小组件时从不显示。
  - Net Worth（新增 `NetWorth.test.tsx`）：完整走一遍 issue 中的用户场景，并测试移动端标题。

## Design decisions

- 只显示提示，不阻止用户离开页面（沿用 #96 的设计决定），因此不修改 `App.tsx` 或路由。
- 相对日期范围比较的是"范围设置"，而不是它解析出的具体日期：
  - 滑动窗口比较窗口长度。
  - "全部时间"和"上个月""今年至今"等命名范围只比较模式。
  - 固定范围比较具体日期。
  - 因此，保存为"最近 6 个月"的小组件在下个月打开时不会显示为已修改。
- 比较的基准是从服务器获取的已保存小组件：保存成功会刷新数据，标签随之消失；保存失败不刷新，标签保留。

- Calendar 从卡片点击某一天打开时附加的日期筛选会被视为修改，因为 "Save widget" 会保存它。

```markdown
## Description

Adds a "(modified)" label to eight dashboard reports: Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar and Goal. The label appears next to the widget name whenever the report's current settings differ from the saved widget, matching the label Custom Reports already show. It disappears when the user changes the settings back, or after "Save widget" succeeds.

- Adds a shared change-check helper, `widgetModified.ts`, plus the label components `ModifiedLabel.tsx` and `ReportWidgetTitle.tsx`. Custom Reports now reuse the same label component.
- Each report gets a `*WidgetSettings.ts` module. What "Save widget" writes and what gets compared come from the same function, so the label only reacts to settings that are actually saved.
- AI tools (Claude Code) wrote a significant part of this change.

## Related issue(s)

Closes #125

## Testing

- New unit test files for the shared helper and each of the eight reports. Each report's test pins the list of settings "Save widget" writes, checks that changing each one shows the label, and checks that renaming does not.
- Page tests:
  - Goal (extended existing tests): the label appears, disappears after a successful save, stays after a failed save, doesn't appear for a rename alone, and never appears without a widget.
  - Net Worth (new `NetWorth.test.tsx`): walks through the issue's user scenario, plus the mobile header.
- Ran StrykerJS mutation testing on the nine new modules. 26 mutants survived the first run. After adding tests and removing code that had no effect, all nine modules score 100%, with every mutant killed by a test failure rather than a timeout.
- `yarn typecheck` and lint pass, and all report tests pass (15 files, 338 tests).
- Manual testing: not yet checked by hand in the demo budget ("View demo").

## Design decisions

- Show that changes are unsaved instead of blocking the user from leaving (the decision from #96). No changes to `App.tsx` or the router.
- Relative date ranges compare the range *setting*, not the dates it currently resolves to:
  - Sliding windows compare their length.
  - "All time" and named ranges such as "last month" or "year to date" compare only the mode.
  - Fixed ranges compare the exact dates.
  - So a widget saved as "last 6 months" won't show as modified when opened next month.
- The baseline is the saved widget fetched from the server. A successful save refreshes it, so the label disappears; a failed save doesn't, so the label stays.
- Each page waits until its saved settings have loaded before comparing, so the label doesn't flash during loading.
- On Calendar, the date filter added by clicking a day on the dashboard card counts as a change, because "Save widget" would save it.
- Renaming a Summary widget now saves only the name. Previously it also saved any unsaved "Show as" changes. This matches the other seven reports.
- "Save widget" stays enabled even when nothing has changed.
- Crossover adjusts the saved range when it opens: sliding windows move back a month, and ranges are fitted to the months that have data. That logic moved into `crossoverWidgetSettings.ts` so the page and the comparison share it.

## Scope:

- Included: the eight reports listed above, in both the desktop and mobile headers.
- Not included: Formula and the experimental reports (#126), Custom Reports (they already have the label), any prompt when leaving the page, and any change to `App.tsx` or the router.

## Tests:

- `widgetModified.test.ts`: time-range comparison (each mode, day vs month windows, defaults), filter defaults, and when `isWidgetModified` returns early.
- `*WidgetSettings.test.ts` (one per report):
  - Compared settings match saved settings, each setting's change is detected, the name is ignored, and empty settings match the defaults.
  - Report-specific cases: Spending's live comparisons, Summary's "Show as" content, and Crossover's range adjustment and category/account order.
- `GoalReport.test.tsx`, `NetWorth.test.tsx`: the page-level behaviour described above.

## Tech Debt

### Introduced:

- Eight small settings modules. Some defaults (for example Crossover's and Spending's) exist both in the page's setup code and in the comparison, so changing one means updating the other.
- Each page has a new `isRangeReady` state to wait for the saved date range to load.
- Only Goal and Net Worth have page-level tests; the other six reports have unit tests only.

### Existing:

- Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover and Calendar may stay stuck on the loading indicator when opened without a widget id (for example `/reports/cash-flow`). Not verified, and not fixed here.

D6 - Mutation Testing (new)¶
This is a new individual deliverable.

What it is. A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (mutants), such as flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is killed. If all tests pass, the mutant survived: your tests did not notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.

What to do. For one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two such issues; your small issue may be one of them):

Run a mutation testing tool on the source files changed by your PR(s) for that issue. Do not run it on the whole project.
Using the tool's report, analyze every surviving mutant: is it equivalent (it behaves exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a gap in your tests? If there are more than 10 surviving mutants, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines your PR added or changed.
Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a surviving mutant that revealed a gap. Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no surviving mutant reveals a gap (all are killed or equivalent), say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
Answer the questions in the template below.
Evidence. Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (StrykerJS: add "json" to reporters; Gremlins: --output=<file>.json; go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file). Commit the report from your first run and from your re-run as docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json and -after.json (.txt for go-mutesting). The mutation scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.

A tool is required. Manual mutation does not count.

Stack	Tool
TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest (Actual Budget, Cal.diy, Excalidraw, Outline, Gitea frontend)	StrykerJS with the Vitest runner
TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa)	StrykerJS with the Jest runner
Go (Gitea backend)	Gremlins or go-mutesting
Set it up early. Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services, and choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits the configuration they used. You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to), as long as you run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.

Common problems to watch for:

The tool stops before mutating. Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any of the selected tests fail, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where your baseline run helps).
Tests run against built code. If your tests run against compiled output (for example, a dist folder) instead of the source, mutants in the source are never seen by the tests. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing, or choose tests that run on source.
Tests need services. Some test suites need a database or another service running. Start them before running the tool.
False survivors. If you limit which tests run (for example, with Vitest's dir option), make sure the tests that cover the mutated files are included. Otherwise, mutants that some test would catch are reported as survived or not covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
Long runs. Mutating only the files changed by your PR keeps run time manageable.
If you are blocked

If you cannot get the tool to run, first ask your teammates: someone may already have a working setup. If you are still stuck, tell the TA as early as possible, with the errors you got and the AI log of what you tried. The TA will help you debug it. If it still cannot be made to work, the TA may approve running the tool on a different issue or a different part of your code instead. Problems reported at the end of the sprint will not excuse a missing D6.

468:The difference is that `checkout` does two unrelated jobs:
472:Because one command does both, a typo or a file named like a branch can wipe out work you meant to keep. Git 2.23 (2019) split `checkout` into two safer commands: `git switch` for branches and `git restore` for files. `switch` only ever changes branches, so it can't discard edits by accident. If your friend's Git is older than 2.23, `checkout -b` works the same way.
479:- **`@stryker-mutator/core`** is the engine and the `stryker` command. It copies the project into a sandbox, creates *mutants* (small deliberate bugs, like changing `>` to `>=` or `+` to `-`), runs your tests against each one, and writes the reports.
480:- **`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner`** is a plugin that lets Stryker run tests with **Vitest**, which is what this repo uses. It also tracks which tests cover which lines, so each mutant only runs the tests that matter.
484:**Why not `npx stryker init`:** Init runs its own install commands, which can be unreliable in a Yarn 4 monorepo and may put packages in the wrong `package.json`. Installing by hand also shows you what each piece does, which helps when you explain it to someone else.

506:- **Peer dependency warnings** (codes like `YN0060` or `YN0002`) are usually fine. They're warnings, not errors.
507:- **The two Stryker packages must be the same major version.** Installing them together in one command makes sure of that. If a friend adds them one at a time later, the versions can drift apart, and Stryker will refuse to load the plugin.

// Vitest config for mutation testing the "(modified)" label (issue #125) with
// StrykerJS. Used by stryker.config.json.
//
// A standalone config rather than the full vite.config.mts: that config
// copies public assets every time it loads, which fails when Stryker's
// parallel workers load it at the same time. These unit tests only need
// module resolution and the test-mode clock.
import { readdirSync } from 'node:fs';

import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

// Stryker's Vitest runner adds its setup file (stryker-setup-<n>.js, written
// into the sandbox) to the config only after Vitest has started. Vitest 5
// never loads it, so mutants are never switched on and every mutant is
// reported as surviving. Listing the file here makes Vitest load it. All
// copies are identical, so any one will do.
const strykerSetupFile = readdirSync(process.cwd()).find(file =>
  /^stryker-setup-\d+\.js$/.test(file),
);

export default defineConfig({
  resolve: {
    conditions: ['electron-renderer', 'module', 'browser', 'default'],
    tsconfigPaths: true,
  },
  test: {
    include: [
      'src/components/reports/widgetModified.test.ts',
      'src/components/reports/reports/*WidgetSettings.test.ts',
    ],
    environment: 'node',
    globals: true,
    setupFiles: [
      ...(strykerSetupFile ? [`./${strykerSetupFile}`] : []),
      './vitest.stryker.setup.ts',
    ],
  },
});

```

export function toComparableSpendingSettings(
  meta: Partial<SpendingMeta> | null | undefined,
) {
  const isLive = meta?.isLive ?? true;
  const mode = meta?.mode ?? 'single-month';
  // Resolve the months the same way the report does when it opens, so a
  // widget without saved months compares equal to the defaults it shows.
  // This also ignores the second month of a live budget or average

    isLive,
    mode,
  };

# Mutation testing: Issue #125 -- Show a "(modified)" label on the standard report widgets

**PR(s):** #163  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.0.0 (command runner; see [Setup notes](#setup-notes))  **Config:** [`packages/desktop-client/stryker.config.json`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/blob/87dc81a369ee959b8ac3c8825f97319fad854e67/packages/desktop-client/stryker.config.json) and [`vitest.stryker.config.mts`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/blob/87dc81a369ee959b8ac3c8825f97319fad854e67/packages/desktop-client/vitest.stryker.config.mts), based on my loot-core setup from #91  **Command:** `cd packages/desktop-client && npx stryker run`
**Reports:** [before](reports/125-bennettmatuszewski-before.json) · [after](reports/125-bennettmatuszewski-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 88.62% → after 100.00%

| | Mutants | Killed | Timed out | Survived | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 246 | 210 | 8 | 28 | 88.62% |

Stryker counts timed-out mutants as detected, so the before score is (210 + 8) / 246. The after run has 9 fewer mutants because I deleted code that three of the survivors showed had no effect (see the Spending and Crossover rows below).

**What was mutated.** The PR's change-detection logic: `widgetModified.ts` (shared helper) and the eight `*WidgetSettings.ts` modules, one per report. The PR's edits to the report pages (`NetWorth.tsx`, `CashFlow.tsx`, ...) only wire those modules into the pages. Mutating whole page files would mutate thousands of lines the PR didn't touch, so I left them out.

## Setup notes

- **Vitest runner.** The required Vitest runner (`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0) does not work with the Vitest 5.0.0 the repo moved to in the 2026-10-16 upstream merge. Its initial test run passes (118 tests), but no tests run for any mutant, so every mutant is reported as surviving (14% on my files). I checked this was not my config:
  - I ran my loot-core setup from #91 on `sort-categories.ts`, and the `asc`/`desc` mutants "survived" even though `sort-categories.test.ts` tests both directions.
  - When I switched a mutant on by hand (`__STRYKER_ACTIVE_MUTANT__=239`), the tests killed it.
- **Command runner instead.** I used Stryker's command runner, which starts Vitest once per mutant. It is still StrykerJS, but it is not the Vitest runner, so this deviation needs the TA's OK.
- **Standalone Vitest config.** `vitest.stryker.config.mts` runs only the 9 unit test files for these modules. The full `vite.config.mts` copies `public/` assets on every load, which fails with EPERM when Stryker's parallel workers load it at once.
- **Before report.** I deleted the report from my first run during clean-up. So `-before.json` is a second run of that same state: I temporarily undid the 3 code simplifications and removed the tests added after the first run. It matches the first run except that three Crossover mutants at line 43 timed out in the first run and survived in this one.
- **Timeouts.** The before run's 8 timeouts (`widgetModified.ts` lines 37–45) were the machine being overloaded: four Vitest processes, each with several workers. One of them, 39:7 `&&`→`||`, survived in my first run. For the after run I added `--maxWorkers 1` to the Vitest command, and all mutants were killed without timeouts.

## Questions

1. **What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**
   - **Main paths tested; defaults, fallbacks and edges not.** Each report's tests checked that changing every saved setting shows the label. They mostly missed what happens around those settings: values filled in when something isn't saved, fallbacks for bad data, and edge cases in range handling.
   - **Crossover** had the most survivors (12). Its range adjustment (`adjustCrossoverRange`) was only tested indirectly, through cases where both sides went through the same code. When the code under test runs on both sides of a comparison, a bug there cancels out, so the comparison tests could not see it.
   - **Summary** had no test for missing or invalid saved content. It also had none for "Show as" types other than percentage, which the report treats differently.
   - **Dead code.** Three survivors (four mutants) showed code that did nothing (a redundant branch, a redundant sort, an unreachable `?.`). I deleted that code instead of testing it.

2. **Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**
   - **Yes, two of the new tests.** Issue #125's requirements are about when the "(modified)" label shows. They say nothing about logging. The two `parseSummaryContent` tests check that a widget with no saved content logs nothing, and that invalid JSON logs `'Failed to parse widget meta content:'`. Those expected values come from the existing page code's behaviour (the log message was copied from `Summary.tsx`), not from the requirements. I kept them because they pin down the fallback, but they would break on a harmless change to the log wording.
   - **One more is borderline.** `compares settings that are entirely missing` (widgetModified.ts:77) tests robustness: in the app, `isWidgetModified` always gets objects.
   - **Everything else is requirement-based.** The other expected values come from the requirement that the label shows exactly when a setting "Save widget" would save differs from the saved widget.

3. **If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**
   - **What it produced.** I used Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5). It:
     - wrote the Stryker and Vitest configs;
     - diagnosed the Vitest-runner problem;
     - did the first classification of survivors;
     - wrote the new tests and this draft.
   - **What was verified or corrected:**
     - **Fake 14% score.** The first run with the Vitest runner scored 14%. Instead of treating that as real, it inspected the JSON and found `testsCompleted: 0` on every "survived" mutant. It then reproduced the problem on my loot-core setup and confirmed that switching a mutant on by hand killed it.
     - **Wrong "equivalent" call.** Its first analysis called all five Spending line-68 mutants equivalent. While writing this table it found that four of them were real gaps (a live single-month comparison's second month was never tested), added a test, and checked by hand that the test fails against that mutant.
     - **Timeouts.** It noticed that timeouts in the before run were hiding the `widgetModified.ts:39` survivor, and changed the after run so that mutant shows as Killed rather than Timeout.
     - **Before report.** It told me the original first-run report had been deleted, and the before report was regenerated from that same code instead.
     - **My own checks:** that every mutant listed as killed shows `Killed` in the after report, that the scores match both JSON files, and that the full desktop-client report tests pass.
